name: Macrodactyly of Fingers, Unilateral

criteria.description: Unilateral enlargement of one or more fingers involving soft tissue and bone
Progressive disproportionate growth of affected digits compared to contralateral side
No evidence of systemic syndromes or generalized overgrowth disorders
Radiologic evidence of bone hypertrophy and soft tissue overgrowth localized to affected digits

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of unilateral digital enlargement with progressive growth and exclusion of syndromic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

distinguishingFeatures: Asymmetric overgrowth involving multiple body parts
Nerve enlargement with fatty infiltration on imaging
Limb overgrowth involving soft tissue and bone but with vascular anomalies

redFlags: Rapid progression of digit enlargement beyond typical growth patterns
Signs of nerve compression causing significant neurological deficits
Presence of systemic symptoms suggesting syndromic overgrowth
